pairs.why: A has a real dark cast shadow on the grass and a clear light-to-shadow turn on the lid. B's orange body is glossier and flatter, with a hot-spot sheen on the cross.
A's thick rope has soft modeled light, with darker core shadows between the coils and a contact shadow. B is flatter and thinner with little shadow depth.
A has a stronger form turn with a darker underside and a crisp light edge, closer to the real cap's planes. B's shadows are muddy and low contrast.
B has a soft contact shadow under the coil and smoother, rounder light modeling. A floats with no grounding shadow.
B darkens the door top and gives a bit more shadow depth, like the real door's shaded left side and cast shadows. A is lit more evenly.
A has a large soft cast shadow on the floor and darker shadows on the tubes and seat underside, like the real chair. B's shadow is thin and its form is flat.
A has soft contact and cast shadows under the legs and a clear light-to-shadow turn on the tube. B's shading is similar but its grounding is weaker.
A's darker, larger cast shadows around the table and stools match the real card's strong grass shadows. B's shadows are smaller and lighter.
